scope: Selected filters in the Ti64 segmentation examples.

filters.purpose: Load the complete preceding Ti64 checkpoint.
Face-only connectivity on the unchanged BrightOriginal foreground; background stays zero.
Preserve the uint32 label image and copy its values to int32 for indexed core statistics.
Group normalized input intensity by integer region label and count only selected foreground pixels.
Export a normal CSV header and all positive feature ID rows; skip background row zero.
Save all predecessor geometries and arrays together with new labels and measurements.
Load the complete preceding Ti64 checkpoint.
Corner-inclusive connectivity on the unchanged BrightOriginal foreground; background stays zero.
Preserve the uint32 label image and copy its values to int32 for indexed core statistics.
Group normalized input intensity by integer region label and count only selected foreground pixels.
Export a normal CSV header and all positive feature ID rows; skip background row zero.
Save all predecessor geometries and arrays together with new labels and measurements.
Load the complete preceding Ti64 checkpoint.
Flag original face IDs with PixelCount at least 25; this report does not change the label image.
Discard face regions smaller than 25 pixels and sort surviving labels by decreasing size.
Preserve the uint32 label image and copy its values to int32 for indexed core statistics.
Mask nonzero cleaned labels so background pixels never enter per-region intensity statistics.
Group normalized input intensity by integer region label and count only selected foreground pixels.
Create two selection-class rows: zero is the unselected complement and one is selected bright pixels; these are not material phases.
Copy the original binary mask to int32 selection classes 0 and 1 for ensemble statistics; preserve the mask.
Copy the uniform selection class within each original region to its own feature table; this is not intensity aggregation.
Count positive original region IDs by selection class; feature row zero is excluded.
Count original selected pixels over the complete 596 by 596 crop; on this one-slice image the result is a 2D selected-area fraction.
Copy the retained binary mask to int32 selection classes 0 and 1 for ensemble statistics; preserve the mask.
Copy the uniform selection class within each retained region to its own feature table; this is not intensity aggregation.
Count positive retained region IDs by selection class; feature row zero is excluded.
Count retained selected pixels over the complete 596 by 596 crop; on this one-slice image the result is a 2D selected-area fraction.
Bound each retained region in inclusive pixel indices for the 2D moment calculation.
Describe the retained brightness-patch shapes with normalized Omega1, Omega2 and saved central moments; original singleton regions are intentionally not measured.
Label connected components of both 0 and 1 brightness classes with exact integer equality and face adjacency; zero-valued input pixels are eligible because no mask is used.

Count pixels for every two-class component. Preserve this complete feature table as the unmodified class-selection reference; measured foreground intensity summaries remain in the original FaceRegionData.

Assign feature-level brightness classes from the mask, using the feature-sized destination despite its Cell Data parameter label. Exact two-class components guarantee a uniform mask value within each feature.
Record original two-class component IDs, including reserved row zero, so later compacted feature rows remain traceable to their measured pixel sets.
Copy the two-class IDs and their paired feature table before removing the unselected brightness class; preserve the full measured partition.
Flag class-zero components for removal, not as bad measurements. Feature row zero is reserved and ignored by the removal operation.
Drop dark-class component pixels to background zero without copying neighbor attributes; compact the bright-only feature table and carry OriginalComponentId with each surviving row.

Copy the prepared foreground-only IDs and feature table for the independent area-budget comparison. This measured population is equivalent to the new bright-only partition and has a known feature-table shape during preflight.
Record original foreground-only face-region IDs before rank compaction. SourceFaceRegionId indexes FaceRegionData and is a different namespace from the two-class OriginalComponentId.

Keep whole bright components in descending pixel-count order until their cumulative area reaches at least 80 percent of all bright pixels. Include the crossing component; drop the remainder to zero without filling.
Expose the ranked selection as a 0/1 mask for direct comparison with BrightOriginal and the independent 25-pixel LargeRegionMask.
Export positive ranked-region rows with pixel counts, measured intensity statistics, selection class, and SourceFaceRegionId; exclude reserved row zero.
Export a normal CSV header and all positive feature ID rows; skip background row zero.
Save all predecessor geometries and arrays together with new labels and measurements.
